quotes.note: An isolated sentence about an unnamed man as 'he' does not by itself distinguish third-person base narration from a participating narrator describing someone else.
The quotation begins mid-sentence and omits the subject and surrounding scene, so its third-person possessive is not sufficient to identify the base narrator.

This passage names Will Robie, a character from Baldacci's later Will Robie series who cannot belong to the 1997 novel; it is apparent Goodreads attribution contamination rather than narration from The Winner.
Free-indirect exposition presents LuAnn externally as 'LuAnn' while conveying her outlook; the generic 'you' expresses a maxim and is not sustained second-person narration.
The clipped fragment omits its subject and surrounding narration, preventing reliable attribution despite the visible third-person possessive.
The fragment lacks both a complete sentence and enough local context to determine whether it is base narration.
The truncated phrase supplies no narrator, subject, or recoverable quotation boundaries.

web_evidence.title: The Winner by David Baldacci
web_evidence.note: The sustained retail sample opens with externally narrated scenes focalized first through Jackson and then LuAnn, consistently naming them and using he/she while conveying both characters' thoughts; no participating narrator frames either scene.

web_evidence.title: David Baldacci Writing Styles in The Winner
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly states that the novel is written in third-person point of view and distinguishes character dialogue from the supporting narration of scenes, thoughts, and emotions.

web_evidence.title: Psychopathic Disorder in David Baldacci's The Winner
web_evidence.note: This university literary analysis describes narration centered on both Jackson and LuAnn and quotes third-person narrative passages from widely separated interior pages, corroborating a nonparticipating narrator across the novel.

web_evidence.title: The Winner Quotes by David Baldacci
web_evidence.note: The opened quote page verifies the supplied fragments but also attributes a Will Robie passage to this 1997 novel, demonstrating contamination in the quote collection; that passage was excluded from base-person evidence.

search_log: Searched "The Winner" "David Baldacci" with excerpt, first chapter, narrator, point of view, first person, third person, and multiple-perspective terms.
Opened and inspected the sustained BingeBooks sample, which covers consecutive opening scenes centered on Jackson and LuAnn in third person.
Opened BookRags' point-of-view section, which explicitly classifies the whole novel as third person.
Opened a Diponegoro University literary analysis and inspected its descriptions and quoted passages from the beginning and later pages of the novel.

Searched exact supplied quotation strings to verify provenance and context; Goodreads confirmed the fragments, while Bookey's chapter material linked q00004 to LuAnn's third-person interior perspective.
Checked Google Books and publisher/author URLs; Google Books exposed catalog metadata but no readable diagnostic prose, and the publisher and author pages were inaccessible to the research tool.

Exact-string searches for q00003 found the same anomalous Goodreads attribution but no credible placement in The Winner; the presence of Will Robie makes it chronologically and narratively incompatible with the 1997 novel.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person with shifting focalization, including Jackson and LuAnn. The authorized-length opening sample, a scholarly whole-novel analysis, and an explicit whole-book POV description agree, while q00004 independently exhibits third-person free-indirect narration. The generic 'you' in q00004 is a maxim, not second-person storytelling. Most other supplied quotes are too clipped to diagnose person, and q00003 is a misattributed passage from the later Will Robie corpus. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person sections was found.
